subject: general
question: In May 2025, the Ministry of Education launched a nationwide enforcement drive around schools and colleges for what purpose?

options.text: Improving safety measures for female students
Promote positive campus culture and prevent incidents of ragging
Making educational institutions free from tobacco and substance

solution:
The correct answer is __**Making educational institutions free from tobacco and substance.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Purpose of the enforcement drive:** The nationwide enforcement drive initiated by the **Ministry of Education in May 2025** focused on making **educational institutions free from tobacco and substance abuse.** This is part of a larger campaign to promote a healthy and safe environment for students.
 
• The initiative specifically targeted schools and colleges to ensure that young individuals are not exposed to harmful substances like tobacco, drugs, and alcohol. Such exposure can lead to addiction and negative physical and mental health outcomes.
 
• The campaign involved collaboration with authorities, educators, and local stakeholders to ensure effective enforcement and create awareness among students regarding the harmful effects of substance abuse.
 
• This drive aligns with the government's broader goals of promoting public health and ensuring that educational institutions serve as safe spaces for learning and development. The initiative also emphasized preventive measures and counseling for students prone to substance abuse.
 
• Efforts were made to implement strict regulations prohibiting the sale or consumption of tobacco and other harmful substances within a specified radius of schools and colleges.
 
• **Awareness campaigns:** As part of the program, workshops and seminars were organized for students, parents, and teachers to educate them on the **long-term impacts of substance abuse.**
 
• The Ministry ensured that educational institutions actively participated in the drive by introducing policies and monitoring mechanisms to prevent substance abuse.
 
• **Legal support:** The enforcement drive was backed by existing laws and regulations, such as the **Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003**, which prohibits the sale of tobacco products near educational institutions.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Making educational institutions free from tobacco and substance.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003:**

 
 
• **COTPA** prohibits the sale of tobacco products within a **100-meter radius of educational institutions**. This act is crucial for protecting students from exposure to harmful substances.
 
• It mandates strict penalties for violations, including fines and legal action against offenders. It also requires educational institutions to display **anti-tobacco signage** as part of compliance measures.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Tobacco and Substance Abuse:**
 
 
• Substance abuse, especially among young individuals, leads to **serious health problems**, including respiratory issues, cardiovascular diseases, and mental health disorders.
 
• It adversely affects academic performance and social behavior, leading to long-term consequences in personal and professional life.
 
• 
 
• 
• **Global statistics:** According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, tobacco kills more than **8 million people annually**, with many starting its use during adolescence.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Prevent Substance Abuse:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, along with the Ministry of Education, often conducts nationwide campaigns to create awareness about the dangers of substance abuse.
 
• Programs like **National Drug De-addiction Programme** focus on providing counseling and rehabilitation services to students and young individuals.
 
• **Awareness drives:** Schools and colleges conduct regular workshops, street plays, and interactive sessions to educate students and parents about substance abuse.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal and Social Considerations:**

 
 
• Schools and colleges are legally required to enforce a **tobacco-free policy** as per government directives, ensuring compliance with the law.
 
• The Ministry of Education collaborates with local authorities to monitor and enforce rules, ensuring that no illegal sale or consumption takes place near educational institutions.
 
 
 
• **Effective Implementation:**
 
 
• The success of such drives depends on active participation from **educational administrators, parents, and students.** Awareness and education play a crucial role in ensuring compliance and preventing substance abuse.
 
• **Monitoring mechanisms** like CCTV cameras and regular inspections help in identifying and curbing violations effectively.
 
• **Collaboration with NGOs:** Many non-governmental organizations actively support the government by conducting anti-substance campaigns and providing counseling services for affected individuals.
